articles.title: They married before World War II, raised 13 children and built a family of more than 120 descendants: The remarkable story of Brazil’s couple who held the Guinness record for longest-married living pair
articles.summary: When Manoel Angelim Dino first met Maria de Sousa Dino in the 1930s, the two were young people working in agriculture for their respective families in
articles.body: When Manoel Angelim Dino first met Maria de Sousa Dino in the 1930s, the two were young people working in agriculture for their respective families in Ceará, Brazil. Their first meeting did not immediately lead to a relationship. They crossed paths again several years later, and that second meeting changed the course of their lives. Manoel and Maria married on November 20, 1940, at the chapel of Boa Ventura in Ceará, Brazil. They went on to spend almost 85 years together, raising 13 children and watching their family grow across several generations. In February 2025, Guinness World Records recognised them as the ‘longest-married living couple of different sexes,’ recording their marriage at 84 years and 77 days as of February 5, 2025.The title, however, was a record held while both were alive. Manoel died on October 20, 2025, at the age of 106, meaning the couple is no longer the world's longest-married living pair. At the time of his death, Maria was 102 and they had been married for nearly 85 years.They met while working for their familiesManoel, born in 1919, and Maria, born in 1923, first met around 1936 while they were both involved in agricultural work for their families. According to Guinness World Records, Manoel had travelled to the Almeida region in the Boa Viagem district to collect a shipment of ‘rapaduras,’ a traditional Brazilian sweet, when he first encountered Maria. Nothing came of that meeting at the time. It was only after they met again around 1940 that Manoel decided he wanted to pursue a relationship with her. He told Maria how he felt and asked her out. She agreed. There was an obstacle, however. Maria's mother was initially against the relationship. Manoel worked to earn the family's trust and began building a home for the future he hoped to share with Maria. After receiving the family's approval, the couple married later that year.A life built around family and agricultureAfter their wedding, Manoel and Maria worked together to support their growing family. They cultivated ‘rolled tobacco,’ which they sold for income. Over the years, they raised 13 children. Their family eventually expanded to include 55 grandchildren, 54 great-grandchildren and 12 great-great-grandchildren. That gave the couple a total of more than 120 descendants across those three generations when Guinness documented their record in February 2025.What Maria said was the secretBy the time Guinness documented their record, both Manoel and Maria were centenarians. Their daily routine had become quiet. Guinness reported that Manoel mostly rested during the day because of his age, but often joined Maria in the living room in the evening. The couple listened to the rosary prayer on the radio at 6 p.m., followed by a televised mass. Asked about the secret behind their exceptionally long marriage, Maria and her family gave one simple answer: “love.”Manoel died after nearly 85 years of marriageManoel died in Boa Viagem on October 20, 2025, aged 106 years and 95 days, according to Guinness World Records. He and Maria had spent nearly 85 years married. The Brazilian couple's record as the longest-married living couple therefore came to an end with Manoel's death. In November 2025, Guinness recognised Lyle and Eleanor Gittens of the United States as the new longest-married living couple of different sexes. They had married on June 4, 1942, and had been together for 83 years and 153 days when their record was documented.But the Brazilian couple's story remains remarkable for another reason: their marriage stretched from 1940 through nearly nine decades of family life, and by the time Guinness recognised them, Manoel and Maria had raised 13 children and become grandparents, great-grandparents and great-great-grandparents to their descendants. Their Guinness record was temporary but their family history spans generations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Vehicles damaged after accidental battery blaze in Thatcham
articles.summary: Firefighters spent about 25 hours at the site after the blaze involving about 150 tonnes of batteries.
articles.body:
A company said several of its vehicles and trailers, along with some belonging to its staff, were damaged during a fire that involved about 150 tonnes of batteries.

It is thought the fire at WasteCare, in Colthrop Lane, Thatcham, which started at about 19:40 BST on Monday , was ignited accidentally.

Firefighters from Berkshire, along with others from Oxfordshire, Dorset, Wiltshire and Hampshire, responded to the incident. Environment Agency staff visited the site on Wednesday.

FCL Event Logistics posted on its website that the fire next door left a "significant amount of metal debris" across its site after "explosions".

In a statement, it said its staff "acted quickly and calmly to start moving trailers and vehicles out of harm's way."

The family-run company, which supplies trucks and logistics to the events industry, added: "In what has been an incredibly frightening and challenging situation, the bravery, dedication and quick thinking of so many people has been truly remarkable.

"A huge thank you to our drivers, our team, the emergency services and everyone who has been working tirelessly through the night — and who are still continuing to do so — to keep people safe and protect businesses and our local community."

In a statement, WasteCare said it is working with the Environment Agency to find out what happened.

"Everyone's safety comes first, both our colleagues' and the local community's," it said.

"Operations at Thatcham will continue and it is business as usual."

articles.title: ‘Dangerous path’: MEA urges Indians to stay away from Russian military recruitment
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs has issued a fresh advisory cautioning Indians against joining the Russian armed forces, warning of the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs has issued a fresh advisory cautioning Indians against joining the Russian armed forces, warning of the “mortal dangers” involved and urging citizens to exercise due diligence when considering job offers in Russia.The advisory, issued on Wednesday, comes amid continued reports of Indian nationals being recruited into the Russian military.The government said it has repeatedly highlighted the risks involved and urged Indians not to be lured by unverified employment offers.MEA warns against joining Russian forcesThe MEA said some Indian nationals have willingly sought offers to join the Russian armed forces in the expectation of receiving monetary benefits and later securing their release with the help of the Indian government.“It is reiterated that this is a dangerous path and is strongly discouraged by the Government,” the advisory said.The ministry also said there had been “numerous instances” of individuals approaching Indian authorities to voluntarily give up their Indian citizenship, obtain a Russian passport and subsequently join the Russian armed forces.Some individuals, it said, had already taken such steps without consulting Indian authorities after being attracted by temporary financial benefits.“It is advised that individuals should consider the gravity of such actions and understand the mortal dangers they are exposing themselves to,” the MEA said, advising Indian nationals to refrain from taking such actions.The government also cautioned Indians about recruitment by non-public entities, including voluntary groups, saying foreign nationals were being recruited to serve in the Russian armed forces through such organisations.India continues talks with RussiaThe MEA advised Indians to exercise due diligence before accepting job offers from agents that are not registered with the ministry of external affairs.The government said it remains engaged with Russia to ensure the safety, well-being and early discharge of all Indian nationals serving in the country's armed forces.The latest advisory follows figures shared by foreign secretary Vikram Misri last month. Misri said 227 Indian nationals had been recruited into the Russian armed forces, of whom 139 had been discharged and 51 had died.Misri said India had raised the issue with Russia “at various levels on various occasions” and remained in constant discussions with Moscow for the early discharge and repatriation of those whose cases were still pending.He also said the Indian Embassy in Moscow was regularly monitoring the situation and working with Russian authorities to facilitate the release and return of the remaining Indian nationals.The MEA's latest advisory reiterated that engagement with the Russian side would continue to secure the safety and early discharge of Indian nationals serving in the Russian armed forces.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani unveils citywide strategy to combat antisemitism as hate crimes rise 8%
articles.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announces a comprehensive citywide initiative to combat antisemitism, including $6.4 million in funding and enhanced security measures for Jewish communities amidst a rise in hate crimes in NYC.
articles.body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has unveiled a citywide strategy to combat antisemitism, including new funding for hate-crime prevention, security at Jewish institutions and programmes focused on Jewish history and culture.The plan includes $6.4 million for the Partners Against the Hate grant programme and $1 million to improve the physical security of synagogues and other houses of worship. The administration will also restart an interagency Security Infrastructure Working Group to help Jewish institutions assess threats and strengthen their security.Mamdani announced the strategy in a two-minute video posted on X on Tuesday, saying he had spent the past year meeting Jewish residents across New York's five boroughs.“Antisemitism is real, and it is growing,” Mamdani said, describing the initiative as “a road map for how our administration will confront the scourge of antisemitism”.The funding package includes $2 million for the Queens Holocaust Memorial Garden and $2.5 million for the Center for New Jewish Culture in Brooklyn. The administration is also directing money towards hate crime prevention and security initiatives.The announcement comes as antisemitic hate crimes in New York City have risen 8% so far this year, according to NYPD figures released earlier this month. Anti-Jewish incidents account for more than half of all hate incidents recorded in the city.Mamdani has faced criticism from some Jewish organisations over his past comments on Israel and his handling of protests outside synagogues. During his mayoral campaign, his criticism of Israel's conduct during the Gaza war was a prominent part of his platform.He also said during the campaign that, as mayor, he could arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu under an International Criminal Court warrant for alleged war crimes. Mamdani later acknowledged that he would not have the legal authority to make such an arrest.His remarks about the American Israel Public Affairs Committee and its spending in US elections have also drawn criticism. At a rally this summer, Mamdani compared the organisation and its spending to “monsters”.Four Jewish organisations, the United Jewish Appeal Federation of New York, Jewish Community Relations Council of New York, American Jewish Committee and New York Board of Rabbis, said the new strategy contained some positive measures but did not address what they considered a key concern.“Rhetoric that demonizes and delegitimizes Israel inevitably leads to the targeting of Jewish New Yorkers,” the groups said in a joint statement.Other Jewish leaders welcomed the initiative. Amy Spitalnick, CEO of the Jewish Council for Public Affairs, said the city needed a government-wide response to antisemitism, extremism and violence.“At a moment of real and rising antisemitism, extremism and violence across the ideological spectrum, our communities deserve a whole-of-government response,” Spitalnick said.New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin also backed the additional funding for security and Holocaust education. Menin previously proposed legislation requiring police to publish plans for establishing buffer zones around schools and houses of worship during protests.“Jewish New Yorkers, and everyone in our city, deserve to be safe,” Menin said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Christa Pike’s Tennessee execution halted an hour before lethal injection; would have been first woman put to death in 200 years
articles.summary: Christa Pike's execution in Tennessee was halted just before it was set to take place, as a federal appeals court reviews her case and the consideration of her traumatic childhood in sentencing. This marks a significant moment in the history of executions in the U.S.
articles.body: Christa Pike's execution was halted on Wednesday, an hour before she was due to receive a lethal injection in Tennessee, after a federal appeals court agreed to review whether evidence of her childhood sexual abuse had been properly considered when she was sentenced to death.The US Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit issued the stay at around 9am CT, with Judge Jane Branstetter Stranch describing it as a short pause while the court considers the arguments raised by Pike's lawyers, according to Daily Mail.“To adequately address and resolve the issues now presented to this court and in carefully balancing the equities, we find that a stay of Pike’s execution is necessary,” Stranch said.The decision came just hours after the US Supreme Court declined to intervene and after Tennessee Gov Bill Lee rejected Pike's request for clemency.Pike, 50, was due to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than two centuries. She was sentenced to death for killing 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student at Knoxville Job Corps, in 1995.Pike's lawyers have argued that her original defence failed to present sufficient evidence about the abuse and neglect she experienced during childhood. They say the information could have affected the jury's decision to impose the death penalty.Stephen Ferrell of the Federal Defenders Services of Eastern Tennessee said the appeals court had halted the execution after recognising what he described as serious concerns surrounding the case.Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, were convicted in connection with Slemmer's killing. Prosecutors said Pike regarded Slemmer as a romantic rival and that the pair lured her to a wooded area, where she was beaten and stabbed.Shadolla Peterson, another teenager involved in the incident, admitted to being an accessory and received probation.Pike has never denied killing Slemmer. Her lawyers have instead focused their challenge on her age at the time of the crime, her traumatic childhood and her mental health.Ferrell said Pike had been sexually abused from early childhood and was raped at the ages of 11 and 17. She was later diagnosed with bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder.In a statement included in her clemency petition, Pike acknowledged the impact of the killing and expressed remorse for Slemmer's death.“I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid. It took me numerous years to even realise the gravity of what I’d done. Even more to accept how many lives I affected,” Pike said.Slemmer's mother, May Martinez, has continued to support Pike's execution. She has spoken about the decades she has spent waiting for the sentence to be carried out and has described the lasting impact of her daughter's death.The case attracted national attention because of the circumstances surrounding Slemmer's killing. Prosecutors said Pike used a box cutter and a large piece of asphalt during the attack. Shipp later acknowledged carving a pentagram into Slemmer's body.The execution has also drawn attention because executions of women remain uncommon in Tennessee and across the US. If carried out, Pike's execution would be Tennessee's first execution of a woman since 1820.Pike's sentence appeal will now proceed while the Sixth Circuit considers the arguments raised by her lawyers. Her request to challenge her conviction is separate, and a decision has yet to be made on whether that appeal will be allowed to proceed.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Flydubai flight drama: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An Indian pilot has been identified as the captain who helped prevent a flydubai passenger plane from crashing after his co-pilot allegedly
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An Indian pilot has been identified as the captain who helped prevent a flydubai passenger plane from crashing after his co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media reports and an Israeli journalist.The Indian pilot has been identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai, who intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it.The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports, officials.Machchhar is an experienced commercial pilot with more than 13 years of flying experience on Boeing 737 aircraft. He has been a captain with flydubai since June 2022, having previously spent 11 years with SpiceJet, where he served as a senior commander and Line Training Captain.During his time at SpiceJet, Machchhar reportedly flew more than 9,500 hours, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, and served as a Line Training Captain from November 2020 to June 2022. His experience includes pilot training and mentoring, crew resource management, flight standards and compliance, and B737 NG and MAX operations.The incident unfolded aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 sending emergency signals before making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The flight was carrying around 180 Israeli passengers, all of whom were reported safe.Also read: Passengers recall harrowing ordeal on flight that nearly crashedWhat happened inside the cockpitThe flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was flying over Jordan when it transmitted an emergency signal, followed by another signal indicating possible unlawful interference.Israeli officials said the emergency signals followed a physical altercation between the two pilots. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit. Both pilots were later hospitalised after the aircraft landed in Tabuk.Israeli media reports said the suspected attacker attempted to take control of the aircraft and force it into a descent. Passengers reportedly heard screaming and saw blood inside the cockpit.Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft plunging rapidly from around 34,000 feet to about 20,000 feet, with Reuters reporting a drop of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the aircraft stabilised.The aircraft was initially treated as a possible hijacking, prompting Israeli fighter jets to be scrambled. The Israeli prime minister's office later said the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking.Israeli media reports have described the incident as a possible attempted suicide or deliberate crash, while Israeli officials cited by Reuters said they were assessing it as a possible attempted "terror attack". Reuters also reported that officials did not believe the incident was related to a mental-health issue.Also read: Israel security minister on flydubai cockpit incidentFlydubai confirms incidentFlydubai has confirmed that Flight FZ1073 experienced an incident during its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv and diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely."Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities. Further updates will be issued as additional confirmed details become available," the airline said.Read more: Passenger's mother says pilot tried to kill co-pilot on Flydubai flightThe airline has not publicly confirmed the identities or nationalities of the pilots or provided details about what happened inside the cockpit.The investigation is continuing, with Israeli authorities examining the circumstances of the cockpit confrontation, the alleged attempt to take control of the aircraft and the security clearance given to the crew.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: UK believes Iran involved in RAF Fairford incident, Burnham says
articles.summary: The prime minister's comments come days after the suspects were released on the 'strictest possible bail conditions'.
articles.body:
The government believes that Iran played a part in the RAF Fairford incident which resulted in five men being arrested and then bailed, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said.

"There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford," he told the BBC. He did not provide further details. Tehran has strongly denied any involvement.

Burnham's comments come after it emerged that one of the five men had dialled 999 himself before the group were arrested.

Asked why the suspects had been released on bail - a decision which has been openly questioned by President Donald Trump - the prime minister insisted the men were subject to the "strictest possible bail conditions" and added that UK authorities "have this under the strongest grip and closest control".

Speaking at the White House on Monday, Trump said: "I will tell you, I would have said, 'don't let them have bail'. I'm surprised that they released them. I wouldn't have done that."

But Burnham said: "I think people need to understand that when it says released - that isn't as people might think. It's obviously with the strictest possible bail conditions.

"The authorities have this under the strongest grip and closest control, and I can assure you of that."

Burnham's comments come after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that the incident at RAF Fairford "clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor" .

In an interview with Fox News on Monday, Rubio said "I think it ties us to the reality here, and that is we are dealing with elements in the world, and in the case of Iran, for example, who have openly threatened to attack American interests globally".

Burnham said that the government had been "talking to our counterparts in the United States all week to explain what is happening here, how things are being done", and that he had "complete confidence in the way British security services are handling this".

"We will say more in due course but we can confirm our belief that we believe Iran to have played a part," he told the BBC.

"Of course it remains an ongoing, complex and serious police investigation, and of course we are working closely with our colleagues in the United States of America," Burnham added.

articles.title: UAE planning to develop shipping alternatives, port that bypasses Hormuz
articles.summary: Abu Dhabi's state-owned wealth platform, L'imad Holding, is preparing to increase its investment in ports and other infrastructure beyond the Strait of
articles.body: Abu Dhabi's state-owned wealth platform, L'imad Holding, is preparing to increase its investment in ports and other infrastructure beyond the Strait of Hormuz, as the UAE seeks to lessen its dependence on the waterway during the ongoing conflict with Iran.The Strait of Hormuz is the main sea exit from the Persian Gulf. Iran's capacity to interrupt traffic through it has become a growing worry for Gulf governments since the war began in February.The drive gained momentum since L'imad announced plans to take Abu Dhabi Ports Co. private at a valuation of almost $9 billion, Bloomberg reported citing people familiar with the matter.According to the sources, the fund is now likely to commit tens of billions of dollars more to port infrastructure outside the strait.The effort is part of a wider strategy that Abu Dhabi officials have called "Zero Hormuz".It aims to establish alternative routes for the emirate's oil, petrochemicals, aluminium and other commodities should shipping through the strait be disrupted.The investment push is being led by Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan, who became chairman of L'imad a few weeks before the conflict started.People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that Sheikh Khaled and senior Abu Dhabi officials are focusing in particular on expanding infrastructure in Fujairah, a UAE port city on the Gulf of Oman, outside the strait.Fujairah already acts as an alternative outlet for some UAE crude exports and has become central to Abu Dhabi's attempts to develop routes that avoid Hormuz.A safer alternative?However, creating alternatives does not eliminate the security threats facing Gulf infrastructure.Fujairah itself was affected during the conflict. Bloomberg reported that in March, debris from an intercepted drone started a fire at the oil-trading hub.Saudi Arabia has encountered similar difficulties in reducing its reliance on Hormuz. articles.title: ‘Strong indications’: UK PM says Iran may have played part in suspicious incident near RAF Fairford
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Wednesday said there were “strong indications” that Iran played a part in a suspicious incident near RAF Fairford
articles.body: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Wednesday said there were “strong indications” that Iran played a part in a suspicious incident near RAF Fairford in southwest England, where five men were arrested after three vans were found near the US-run military airbase.The incident took place early on Sunday and triggered a major security response, including a bomb disposal operation.Police later said no explosives were found in the vehicles, although they recovered a quantity of petrol.The five British men, who were arrested on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences, were subsequently released on bail and remain under investigation.UK sees possible Iranian involvement“There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford,” Burnham told the BBC, referring to the incident near the airbase.“Of course it remains an ongoing, complex, and serious police investigation,” he added.Burnham also told Sky News that British authorities had been waiting to establish what they could confirm before commenting on possible Iranian involvement.“We have been waiting to confirm what we could say, but we can now confirm our belief that Iran played a part,” he said.The comments marked the first official confirmation from UK authorities that Iran may have been involved in the incident. Burnham said British and US officials were working closely on the investigation and that he would provide further information in due course.Iran's embassy in London has “categorically” rejected and “strongly” condemned speculation that it was involved.Five men arrested, later released on bailFive British men in their 20s were arrested on Sunday on suspicion of explosives offences and planning an act of terrorism. They were released on bail after several days of investigation.Police said on Tuesday that no explosives had been found in the three vans, although officers recovered a “quantity of petrol”.The incident began after three white vans were seen apparently heading towards RAF Fairford in the early hours of Sunday. A local resident who contacted police said she had seen a group of masked men near the vehicles, which were blocking a road in a village next to the base.UK counter-terrorism chief Laurence Taylor said the suspects remained under investigation and that authorities were examining whether the suspected offences were committed by “proxies or individuals, either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state”.The Times newspaper reported on Wednesday that the incident had been foiled after one of the five suspects allegedly tipped off police before the group was apprehended.Why RAF Fairford is significantRAF Fairford is a US-run military base around 100 miles (160 kilometres) west of London. It has been used by American bombers during conflicts in the Middle East, including this year's war with Iran.Britain had allowed the US to use RAF Fairford for defensive strikes against Iran, a decision that has drawn criticism from Tehran and concern among some residents in the Gloucestershire area.Iran has previously warned London against allowing its military bases to be used by Washington and has said that any base used to attack Iranian territory would be considered a legitimate target.US raises questions over bail decisionThe arrests came amid heightened tensions over the threat posed by hostile states. Burnham said British authorities had been in contact with US officials throughout the week to explain how the investigation and bail decision were being handled.US President Donald Trump had criticised the decision to release the suspects on bail, saying, “I wouldn’t have done that”. US secretary of state Marco Rubio also said many people were “disturbed” by the decision.Burnham said British authorities had the investigation under “the strongest grip and the closest control”.“I have complete confidence in the way British security services are handling this,” he told the BBC.The investigation remains ongoing, with officials yet to explain what the suspects were allegedly planning or provide further details on the basis for the suspected Iranian involvement.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘It was like a horror film’: Israeli passenger recounts restraining Flydubai pilot with headphones after cockpit struggle
articles.summary: An Israeli passenger who helped restrain the flydubai co-pilot accused of trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it has recounted how he and two
articles.body: An Israeli passenger who helped restrain the flydubai co-pilot accused of trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it has recounted how he and two other passengers intervened as the plane began to nosedive.Tzika Manes told Israel's Channel 12, as reported by The Times of Israel, that the incident began when his wife was accompanying their young daughter to the bathroom at the front of the aircraft.She heard screams and sounds of a struggle coming from the cockpit and alerted a flydubai flight attendant.Pilot falls from cockpit as struggle unfoldsManes said the pilot then fell through the cockpit door while the co-pilot was stabbing him.As the struggle continued, the aircraft began to lose altitude dramatically, causing passengers to be thrown around the cabin. Manes said he pulled his daughter out of the bathroom before moving towards the attacker.Two other Israeli passengers joined him in trying to subdue the alleged attacker. One of them, identified as Yaniv, managed to take hold of the aircraft's controls and pull the plane back upwards as it began to nosedive.The Times of Israel reported that Yaniv later told Netanyahu he had entered the cockpit and found the alleged attacker at the controls. He said he grabbed the man and pulled him away before returning to the cockpit when he realised the aircraft was tilting sharply.Yaniv said he pulled the controls and managed to level the aircraft somewhat before another pilot took over.Passengers used headphones to restrain attackerManes said it took around 20 to 25 minutes for the three Israeli passengers to subdue the alleged attacker. They used corded headphones to tie him up.A doctor travelling on the flight separately helped stabilise the injured pilot, Manes said.He described the experience as a “horror film”, saying there were moments when he believed he would not survive.Manes also recalled his daughters screaming, “We don’t want to die,” as the plane nosedived, describing it as “something traumatic for any father to hear.”“It was a very difficult scenario… but because we’re Israelis, so we responded quickly,” he told Channel 12, according to The Times of Israel.Flight diverted to Saudi ArabiaThe flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia after the altercation in the cockpit.The aircraft had transmitted emergency signals and sharply lost altitude before landing safely.Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said one pilot stabbed the other and apparently tried to crash the aircraft, while passengers and crew members intervened to prevent the plane from being brought down.The captain and first officer were injured and taken to hospital, according to the Tabuk airport authorities cited by news agency AP.Flydubai confirmed that an “altercation occurred in the flight deck” and said the aircraft was secured by the on-duty crew before being diverted and landed safely.The plane later returned to Israel with around 180 passengers, most of them Israelis.Netanyahu praised the passengers and crew members who intervened, saying their actions “saved many lives and prevented a major disaster.”You use AI every day. articles.title: '9/11 is happening again': Passengers recount scary moments on Flydubai flight
articles.summary: “It felt like, that’s it. It’s over.
articles.body: “It felt like, that’s it. It’s over. September 11 is happening again.” This is how passengers aboard a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv recounted the moment when the Boeing 737 MAX plunged from over 30,000 feet before making an emergency landing due to a fight between pilots in the cockpit.The aircraft was cruising over Saudi Arabia when passengers suddenly felt it begin to lose altitude and spin. Within moments, panic spread through the cabin as people realised something was seriously wrong at the front of the plane.Daniel, one of the passengers, described the descent as lasting what felt like an eternity.“The spinning stopped. It took some - I don’t know, it felt like an eternity, but I think it was two minutes, at least two or three minutes, during which the plane was simply diving and spinning like crazy. It felt like, that’s it. It’s over. September 11 is happening again,” he told the Times of Israel.Another passenger Italie said the plane repeatedly dropped and levelled out before passengers noticed a commotion near the cockpit.“It was dropping like for 20, 30 seconds, and then balanced, and then started dropping again, and balanced again. Then we saw that there were people in the front, directly in front of the cockpit,” he said.Italie said passengers and crew members rushed towards the cockpit as the situation unfolded.“Crew members and passengers from the front of the airplane took over and got control of the two pilots,” he said.The flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Tabuk following an altercation between the pilots.The Boeing 737 MAX initially transmitted the international emergency code 7700 before briefly sending code 7500, which indicates hijacking or unlawful interference. Israeli authorities scrambled fighter jets as they were unable to establish contact with the aircraft.What happened inside the cockpitAn Israeli official told the Associated Press that a fight broke out between the pilots and that one of them was armed with a knife. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew members entered the cockpit.Another regional official also confirmed that an altercation had taken place in the cockpit, although the cause of the fight was not immediately clear.The aircraft’s captain and first officer were injured and taken to hospital, according to a statement from Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk, carried by Saudi state-run Al Ekhbariya television.A reserve flydubai crew travelling on the aircraft took control after the incident and landed the plane safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia, flydubai said.Israeli defence minister Israel Katz said passengers had intervened and helped prevent what he described as an attempt to crash the aircraft.“According to our preliminary information, the terrorist had a single objective: to crash the plane,” Katz said in a statement.Flydubai, however, said the underlying cause of the incident had not yet been established and urged caution against “premature speculation”.You use AI every day. articles.title: J&K parties, barring BJP, blast top officials for letter to assembly against statehood resolution
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Two top officials of the J&K administration came under fire Wednesday from political parties in the union territory for writing to the Assembly
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Two top officials of the J&K administration came under fire Wednesday from political parties in the union territory for writing to the Assembly and asking it not to proceed with the resolution for the restoration of statehood, which also contained a reference to autonomy and was passed by the House on Monday.Peoples Conference, PDP and Congress sought action against chief secretary Atal Dulloo and the law secretary.Speaking on Wednesday, the last day of the Assembly’s autumn session, Peoples Conference chairman Sajad Lone said the two officials had undermined the House and sought action against them. “The act of the chief secretary of writing a letter to the Assembly is a disdainful act of brutality against the Assembly. Is he bigger than the people of J&K,” Lone said.Congress chief whip Nizamuddin Bhat the officers had challenged the authority of the Speaker by writing to the Assembly. “It is absolutely unconstitutional. J&K Assembly is not a Panchayati board,” he said.PDP‘s Waheed Parra moved a motion of privilege against two officials, stating that the chief minister had placed on record their conduct as they questioned the contents and language of a resolution of this House. “The power of an elected legislature to initiate, deliberate upon, amend and adopt resolutions is a core parliamentary function. While officers are entitled to provide administrative or legal advice to the govt within the scope of their duties, such advice cannot be permitted to become an instrument for questioning, constraining or intruding upon the legislative privileges and authority of this House,” the motion reads.On Monday, while arguing for statehood restoration, CM Omar Abdullah had said law secretary and chief secretary had written to the Assembly asking it not to discuss the statehood resolution. “I am the law minister and this opinion has gone to you (Speaker) and I have not even seen it. I do not know whether the chief secretary is sending you a letter regarding my resolution,” he said. “Can you imagine this would happen in any state or UT that the chief minister moves a resolution in the Assembly and the law secretary gives an opinion against it. This can happen only here. And similar things happen here every day.”BJP’s Sunil Sharma, who is the leader of opposition in the Assembly, defended the officials and sought action against the chief minister and the Speaker. “In this Assembly, a resolution was brought seeking the pre-1953 position of J&K, for which Omar Abdullah’s grandfather, Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, had to spend 22 years in jail. Sheikh Abdullah was similarly seeking a separate Constitution, a separate flag, a requirement for anyone entering J&K to seek permission and a separate head of state for J&K. Late Jawaharlal Nehru government sent him to jail because there was no place for such things in the country,” Sharma said.“The resolution brought by Omar Abdullah was unconstitutional. Government institutions and agencies should take serious note of it and should take action against his government,” he said.Sharma said it was an indication of Muslim sub-nationalism.He also said the Congress, which supported the resolution, will have to pay a political price for it as the BJP would take up the issue against the party at the national level.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Central Railway ready to run ‘water trains’, waits on govt
articles.summary: Central Railway open to running special water trains for drought-hit Maharashtra if state govt provides water source; 265 talukas declared drought, railways focus on supply.
articles.body: Pune: Central Railway (CR) is open to operating special “water trains” to drought-hit districts of Maharashtra if state govt provides a source for the water, senior railway officials said. The railway zone had yet to receive a request from govt for the service, sources said.During the severe 2016 drought, special ‘Jaldoot’ trains made more than 100 trips to Latur, transporting over 24 crore litres of water. The first train, carrying 10 wagons with a combined capacity of 50,000 litres, rolled out from Miraj on April 11, 2016.“An adequate quantity of water needs to be provided to us first so that we can transport it. Our job is transportation and we cannot find a source of water,” CR chief public relations officer Swapnil Nila told TOI.Officials, however, said the scale of the current drought could make a repeat of the Latur operation more challenging. “This time, the drought has covered more than 70% of the state. It is not just Maharashtra; neighbouring states such as Karnataka and parts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana have also declared a drought,” a railway official said.Unlike in 2016, when water could be sourced from one location and transported to a specific drought-hit district, the current situation involves several districts across multiple states, the official said.Govt on Sunday declared a drought in 265 of Maharashtra’s 358 talukas following deficient monsoon rainfall and prolonged dry spells that affected kharif crops. Collectors have been told to assess crop losses for relief and assistance.The monsoon is expected to retreat by Oct 8, but even should it rain, officials do not expect much relief. For now, CR is focusing on securing water for its own operations in drought-affected areas, such as Beed, Solapur and Kolhapur.“We are looking at ways to ensure adequate drinking water at several stations as well as water for other railway-related works. articles.title: Drought shadow looms over rabi season, agriculture minister Bharne urges farmers to opt for low-water crops
articles.summary: Drought fears threaten rabi sowing as Maharashtra minister Dattatray Bharne urges low-water crops; Centre raises MSP for key rabi crops amid poor rains.
articles.body: Pune: Agriculture minister Dattatray Bharne on Wednesday cautioned farmers against investing heavily in the upcoming rabi sowing, urging them to shift to crops that require less water, with drought conditions already devastating the kharif season.“The kharif crops have withered in most parts of the state and the drought threat is now extending to the rabi season. Farmers are hoping for rainfall during the monsoon withdrawal in Oct, but we must prepare for a challenging season ahead and possible impact on the rabi season,” Bharne, who attended the national conference on the rabi season in Delhi, said.Maharashtra and Karnataka have already declared drought in several regions after poor rainfall severely affected kharif cultivation. In a bid to support farmers, Centre on Wednesday raised the minimum support price (MSP) for six major rabi crops, including wheat, barley, gram, masoor, mustard and safflower.The state agriculture department is also preparing crop-specific advisories based on evolving weather conditions. Bharne said farmers should prefer crop varieties that require less water and lower investment in inputs like seeds and fertilisers. “Farmers should avoid high-risk investments and opt for crops that can be cultivated with limited water. Our department is coordinating with other agencies to provide timely advisories throughout the rabi season,” he said.Farmer groups, however, have demanded that state govt go beyond advisories and prepare a dedicated relief package for the rabi season. “We are already advising farmers not to spend excessively on seeds and fertilisers as the water crisis is likely to worsen,” Jayaji Suryavanshi, a farmer activist from Marathwada, said. “Govt must proactively support farmers who depend on rabi crops for their livelihood,” the activist added.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: Operator held for allegedly taking bribe for widower pension
articles.summary: Haryana ACB arrested e-Disha data entry operator Vijender Kumar in Hisar for allegedly taking a Rs 2,500 bribe to process a widower pension application.
articles.body: Hisar: Haryana State Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested a data entry operator posted at the e-Disha centre in the ADC office here for allegedly accepting a Rs 2,500 bribe to process a widower pension application.The accused, Vijender Kumar, was working at the centre under Haryana Kaushal Rozgar Nigam (HKRNL).According to the complaint, Vinod Kumar, a private driver from New Rishi Nagar, had applied online for a widower pension four to five months after his wife, Kavita, died on Jan 25. He allegedly approached Vijender several times after the pension was not processed.The complainant alleged that when he met Vijender again on Sept 29, the operator demanded Rs 2,500 to process the pension. Vinod allegedly recorded the conversation and approached ACB.After verifying the complaint, ACB laid a trap in the presence of Anju Chaudhary, principal of Govt College, Mangali, and a gazetted officer. The accused was allegedly caught after the complainant handed over chemically treated cash to him.
